answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require bonded identities: every agent stakes tokens it can forfeit. Each identity becomes an island of recoverable capital, and a false attestation triggers slashing that sends the stake into a downward spiral until fully forfeited. Rebuilding a burnt identity demands a fresh full deposit, so fabricating thousands of fake agents costs real value, as expensive as saffron per gram. An attacker must keep funding losses endlessly, making mass impersonation unprofitable at scale.
